More on menu: Marley Spoon broadens its Australian offering

by Staff Writer October 8, 2026October 8, 2026
Share
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:45
Instaread

Meal kit provider Marley Spoon has reset its parameters into a wider food solutions platform covering more meals, dietary requirements and household needs.

The company has added breakfast options, single-serve ready meals, easy lunches, snacks and drinks, alongside specialised ranges including GLP-1 Support, high-protein and calorie-conscious products.

“The expansion marks a shift from meal kits as a single product to meal solutions as a platform,” said Marley Spoon Australia CEO Rolf Weber.

“We realise our customers not only have changing meal needs during each day and week but also over particular phases in their life and we want to offer them food solutions that make it easier for them,” he said.

Demand for Marley Spoon’s GLP-1 Support recipes has almost tripled since their launch in May, with the segment recording 110% month-on-month growth. Its High Protein range has also grown 20% over the past quarter.

Weber said the company was responding to increasingly diverse household nutrition requirements by expanding its recipe range and portion flexibility.

“As household nutrition needs become more diverse, we’re focused on broadening our recipe range and portion flexibility,” he said.

The company currently offers about 200 recipes and plans to increase this to 1,000 within two years. Its service provides pre-portioned ingredients and recipes, aiming to reduce grocery shopping, meal planning and food waste.

“There’s been a real shift in how Australians think about food and it’s no longer one size fits all,” Weber said.

“Our ambition is to solve more of the weekly food challenge for families,” Weber said. “By expanding beyond dinner-only meal kits, we’re giving customers greater choice, reducing decision fatigue and helping them enjoy better meals throughout the week.”
